title: Bitcoin chatgpt coach: experience sharing?
author: Estonian_thinker_f
selftext: I'm in a challenge to learn bitcoin basics with 1000 euro. I've set up a "project" in chatgpt with three roles. A trading strategy coach, a daily coach, and a research sparring partner. The strategy chat makes the overall trading method and manages a dashboard and prompt the daily coach. The daily coach gets screen shots and tells me what limit orders. The research chat is where I ask random questions and simulations.  So far, it's been very good in preventing mistakes and less good at opportunities.   Am I on the right track or is this a totally wrong start?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the daily coach reading screenshots is the weak link. it can misread a price off a chart and hand you a limit order that looks reasonable. I'd have it log every order with the price it saw, then check a week of those against the real candles.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The screenshot-reading coach is the weak link, it'll misread a wick and hand you a limit order that looks fine. Log every order with the price it saw and check it against real candles. ChatGPT is decent at stopping dumb trades, bad at spotting entries.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: You're on a sensible track, especially because you're using it to prevent mistakes and not to chase trades. Two things I'd add. First, screenshots are a weak input: the model can misread a level or a candle, so also paste the actual numbers (price, the level, the size) and have it repeat them back before it suggests an order. Second, keep a plain log of every suggestion it made, what you did and what happened, and compare after a month with simply buying a fixed amount weekly, since that shows if the coaching adds anything. With 1,000 euros, fees and spreads also matter more than they seem, so check them on each limit order. Cymetica's Crypto Outlook is one place to look at modeled price ranges for a coin, which helps with how far to place a limit order.

comments.author: Key-Enthusiasm-3403
comments.body:
the screenshot thing is covered so one more way to test it: make the coach commit to a direction before each limit order, up or down or stay out, and score it later against what price actually did. 30 or so calls is enough to see if its entries beat a coin flip. my guess is it wont, which would match what you said, good at stopping dumb trades and not so good at finding good ones. that doesnt make it useless, the stopping part is worth a lot
